policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'his wife also being privy to it' supplies the possessive that English requires with a kinship noun; the Greek article alone carries it as readily as an added αὐτοῦ, so the English does not distinguish the readings.

Presence or absence of the article with Πέτρος has no English exponent; 'But Peter said' is the same either way. The verse note is classed alternative_rendering (Or, deceive) and bears on English wording, not on the reading.

The added σε would be the accusative subject/object within the infinitive clause; ASV 'and to keep back part of the price of the land' leaves the actor unexpressed because the infinitive is already governed by 'thy heart', so neither reading is excluded.

ASV closes with 'all that heard it' — a bare resumptive pronoun. Where this verse does render a demonstrative it says so ('these words' for τοὺς λόγους τούτους), so an added ταῦτα would have surfaced as 'these things', as ASV renders ταῦτα elsewhere.
πρὸς αὐτήν and the dative αὐτῇ both yield ASV 'answered unto her'; the construction leaves no English trace.
The article with the proper name Πέτρος has no English exponent; 'And Peter answered' renders either reading.

ASV 'But Peter said unto her' supplies a verb of speaking that English requires whether εἶπεν stands in the text or is elided after ὁ δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν; the briefing shows no italic supply marking to settle which.
πρὸς τοὺς πόδας and παρὰ τοὺς πόδας alike give ASV 'at his feet'; the preposition is not distinguished in the English.
The variants differ only in the order of πολλά and ἐν τῷ λαῷ; ASV 'many signs and wonders wrought among the people' follows English order regardless.
ἅπαντες and πάντες are both rendered 'they were all'; ASV marks no intensive distinction.

ASV 'they even carried out the sick into the streets' renders both the ascensive καί ('even') and the goal preposition εἰς ('into'); κατὰ τὰς πλατείας would give a distributive 'in/along the streets' and would leave 'even' without a source.
κλιναρίων and κλινῶν both surface as 'beds' in the pair 'beds and couches'; the note 'Or, pallets' is classed alternative_rendering and attaches to κραβάττων, not to this unit.
Aorist subjunctive ἐπισκιάσῃ and future indicative ἐπισκιάσει after ἵνα are both rendered by ASV's 'might overshadow'; English purpose clauses do not distinguish them.

ASV 'the multitude from the cities round about Jerusalem' construes Jerusalem as the point the cities lie round about — the genitive of the base reading. The added εἰς would make Jerusalem the destination of συνήρχετο ('came together ... to Jerusalem'), which ASV does not say.
ASV 'and laid hands on the apostles' carries no possessive; an added αὐτῶν would be rendered 'their hands', as ASV renders possessive genitives with body parts elsewhere.
διὰ νυκτός with or without the article is 'by night' in English; the article has no exponent in the ASV.

ASV coordinates three finite verbs — 'opened the prison doors, and brought them out, and said' — which the participle ἀνοίξας (r02) would instead subordinate ('having opened ... brought'), so r02 is excluded. Between the remaining readings the difference is only the movable nu, invisible in English.
The variants differ only in whether the participle precedes or follows ὑπηρέται; ASV 'the officers that came' places the relative clause after the noun by English rule either way.

The added μέν is a correlative particle ASV routinely leaves unrendered; 'The prison-house we found shut in all safety ... but when we had opened' carries the adversative on 'but' whether or not μέν stood in the protasis.
ASV has the keepers 'standing at the doors' — the locative ἐπί. The variant πρό is spatial 'before/in front of', which ASV renders 'before' (as KJV does here), not 'at'.

ASV names two hearers, 'the captain of the temple and the chief priests'. The variant prefixes a third, ὁ ἱερεύς ('the priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests'), which has no counterpart in the ASV.
ASV 'went the captain with the officers, and brought them' is a simple past that renders either the aorist ἤγαγεν or the imperfect ἦγεν; ASV does not force a progressive here.
μή and ἵνα μή both yield ASV's 'lest they should be stoned'; the fear-clause conjunction is not distinguished in English.

ASV renders a declarative charge, 'We strictly charged you not to teach in this name'. The added Οὐ makes the sentence an interrogative expecting assent ('Did we not strictly charge you?'), which ASV does not have.

The articular infinitive τοῦ δοῦναι and bare δοῦναι are both rendered 'to give repentance'; the article has no English exponent. The note 'Or, at' is classed alternative_rendering and bears on 'with his right hand'.

ASV reads 'And we are witnesses of these things', with no possessive qualifying 'witnesses'; the added αὐτοῦ would give 'we are his witnesses'. The verse's textual_variant notes concern an addition 'in him' and a recast of the Holy Spirit clause, neither of which is this unit's candidate.
ASV 'and so is the Holy Spirit' supplies the elided verb; the connective καί ... δέ and bare καί are both covered by 'and', and ASV adds no 'also' that would settle which stood in the text.
Aorist ἀκούσαντες and present ἀκούοντες both give ASV's 'when they heard this'; the temporal clause does not mark the participle's aspect.
βραχύ and βραχύ τι are both 'a little while'; the indefinite τι adds nothing ASV distinguishes.
ASV 'commanded to put the men forth a little while' renders ἀνθρώπους; the variant ἀποστόλους would be 'the apostles', as ASV renders that noun consistently.

ASV 'to whom a number of men ... joined themselves' fits προσεκλίθη ('inclined toward') and equally the variant προσεκλήθη, which KJV renders with the same 'joined themselves'; the English does not separate them.
The readings differ in the order of ἀνδρῶν and ἀριθμός and between ὡς and ὡσεί; ASV 'a number of men, about four hundred' renders both approximating particles alike and follows English order.
ASV 'drew away some of the people after him' has a partitive with no quantifier; the added ἱκανόν means a considerable number and is rendered 'much people' (KJV), which ASV does not say.
ἄφετε and ἐάσατε are synonyms in this idiom, both rendered 'let them alone'; the ASV wording does not distinguish the verbs.
ASV 'if this counsel or this work be of men' renders a demonstrative with 'counsel' as well as with 'work'; the omission of αὕτη would leave 'the counsel' undetermined.
ASV 'ye will not be able to overthrow them' is future, rendering δυνήσεσθε; the present δύνασθε is rendered 'ye cannot' (KJV).
ASV's object is plural, 'to overthrow them', matching αὐτούς; the neuter singular αὐτό would refer to the counsel or work and be rendered 'it'.
ASV 'and let them go' supplies the object English requires with 'let go'; the pronoun is equally available from the context, so an explicit αὐτούς is not distinguished.
ASV ends 'to suffer dishonor for the Name' — the Name absolute, with no genitive. The variant adds τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, which would be rendered 'for the name of Jesus' or 'his name'.

ASV 'to preach Jesus as the Christ' takes one member as object and the other as predicate, a construal available from either order of τὸν χριστόν and Ἰησοῦν; the English word order follows the sense, not the Greek sequence. The verse's remaining note is a greek_gloss on 'preach'.
